sources.revision: Not stated in document. Filename says v2025.1. Copyright 2025.
sources.location: PDF p. 1, features and standard sizes. PDF p. 2, Performance Data and Radiation Degradation tables.

supportedConfigurations: One 26.5 cm² cell, 6.9 × 3.9 cm standard format. Larger CTJ30 formats and CTJ30-Thin are outside this record.
products.accountingBoundary: One bare 26.5 cm² cell. No bypass diode, coverglass, interconnects, panel, packaging or harness included. Active area is smaller than the rectangular envelope.
caveats: EOL Vmp and Imp are not supplied. Radiation remaining factors are retained separately and are not used to fabricate absolute EOL MPP ratings.
The performance table gives average BOL efficiency 29.1%, the feature headline says 29.5%, and the illustrative I–V curve says 29.7%. The catalog uses the explicitly tabulated performance case.
Independently rounded table averages give Pmax density 39.8 mW/cm² versus Vm × Jm = 39.33 mW/cm². Both are retained without forcing equality.
The source has no visible revision label. v2025.1 is a filename label, not a confirmed hardware revision.

sources.title: NanoPower BP8 100 Wh Datasheet
sources.location: Printed pp. 1–13 (PDF pp. 5–17). Tables 2.1–2.2, pp. 5–6. Table 4.1, p. 11.

supportedConfigurations: Factory 8S1P pack. One pack in this record. Two packs may be paralleled using the manufacturer’s wiring and manual. No series reconfiguration inferred.
products.accountingBoundary: One complete BP8 pack including cells, protection, balancing, telemetry electronics and heater. EPS/P80, harness, mating connectors and spacecraft structure are external. Pack electronics and heater mass are not additional installed products.
caveats: 86 Wh is typical over 23.6–32.0 V. It is not guaranteed minimum usable energy and is not an EOL capacity.
The 100 Wh and 3.5 Ah headline values use a different/full capacity case. They are retained separately and not substituted into the recommended-range energy field.
Cycle-life domain and aging/efficiency models are missing. Telemetry SoC capability does not supply a charge-state model for the demo.
Protection thresholds differ from recommended operating limits. Absolute maxima must not be treated as the normal operating interval.

The 4S2P 6 A charge limit must not be used for this 8S1P record, whose charge limit is 3.4 A.
Cycle life, EOL retention and separate energy/coulombic efficiencies are unavailable.

sources.title: NanoPower P80 Datasheet
sources.location: Printed pp. 1–23 (PDF pp. 8–30). Tables 1.1–1.2 pp. 5–6. Table 2.2 pp. 7–8. Table 4.1 p. 22.

supportedConfigurations: Configuration 1 only: 1×PMU, 1×ACU, 1×PDU in enclosure. ACU has 12 PV inputs in two banks of six MPPT boost converters.

PDU channel-to-regulator assignments are factory hardware configuration. Regulated and raw-battery outputs coexist. Other P80 stack configurations have different mass/envelopes and are outside this record.
products.accountingBoundary: One complete configuration-1 assembly including PMU, ACU, PDU, enclosure and internal electronics. All conditioning/distribution/processor allocations reference this same physical usage and contribute its 0.3608 kg once. BP8 battery, external harness, mating connectors and spacecraft mounting are separate.
caveats: Canonical level board represents a multi-board enclosed assembly here, not a single PCB. Configuration 1 must remain fixed for these physical values.
The datasheet explicitly excludes BP8 from the P80 EPS boundary (printed p. 2). Do not add a battery role or battery capacity to P80.
25 V PV input maximum is distinct from the additional Voc < max(VBAT) condition. No minimum/startup/tracking envelope or aggregate input-power limit is inferred.
Regulator efficiency is supplied as typical curves versus load and battery voltage, not one guaranteed system efficiency. No scalar is adopted.
MCUs and watchdogs are explicit. MCU model, memory, compute headroom and firmware release/timing evidence are missing. No independent software role is claimed.

sources.title: ISISPACE Compact EPS 2, ICEPS2 Datasheet
sources.location: PDF/printed pp. 1–10. Type definitions p. 6. Table 2 electrical/physical specifications pp. 7–9.

supportedConfigurations: Type A only: PIU mainboard + top-mounted PBP-2S1P battery. DaughterBoard is not compatible with this Type A arrangement.
Three mainboard MPPT channels and 3.3 V, 5 V and raw-battery domains. Custom cell or rail options need a separately characterized record.
products.accountingBoundary: One complete Type A PIU + PBP-2S1P assembly. Battery cells, board, heater and integrated MCUs are inside the 184 g typical assembly mass. Count the product once across battery/conditioning/distribution/processor roles. The envelope explicitly excludes CSKB, while the mass table gives no CSKB breakout. EGSE, harness and separately sold stack frames are external.
caveats: Capacity is internally inconsistent. Page 2 advertises 28.2–57.6 Wh and a 7.2 V / 28.8 Wh two-cell option. Table 2 gives default cells 3.2 Ah, which implies 23.04 nominal Wh for 2S at 3.6 V/cell. No energyWh value is adopted.
The charge/discharge current row has Min/Typ/Max values without an explicit safe pack-current envelope. The full tuple is retained, while generic maximum charge/discharge fields remain unresolved.
MPPT functional range is 3.5–7.5 V for Type A. The separate 15 V absolute maximum is not the tracking limit. Above the functional range, power can pass without boost tracking per footnote 12.
Storage recoverability ≥80% is a storage-condition statement, not an orbital cycle-life or EOL retention factor.
MCUs and FRAM are explicitly documented. Firmware version, available processor/memory resources and scheduling evidence are missing. No software role is claimed.

caveats: 1E15 means the named 1 MeV electron/cm² endpoint, not one mission-year or any mapped orbit lifetime.
The 32% family name is not the adopted electrical-table efficiency. Bare-cell efficiency at the specified 1367 W/m² case is 31.3%.
Electrical values and coefficients are typical. The average-weight ≤ statement does not guarantee every individual cell mass.
The electrical table uses 25 °C. The temperature-coefficient domain is 28–140 °C. The 25–28 °C gap and reference applicability must be reviewed before temperature-adjusted prediction.
Page 1 gives CIC glass size 31.42 cm² while p. 2 gives 31.34 cm². This bare-cell record uses the consistent 30.60 cm² cell area and neither glass value.
Full I–V and irradiance-dependent characterization is absent in this short public datasheet. MPP endpoints do not characterize DET operation or partial shading.

supportedConfigurations: One 27 cm² standard rectangular bare cell. Published thickness options span 140–225 µm. No exact thickness-to-mass option mapping or numeric ordering code is stated. Other sizes, CIC assemblies, panels and the older 80–225 µm revision are excluded.
products.accountingBoundary: One 27 cm² bare cell. No coverglass, bypass diode, interconnects, substrate, panel, external blocking diode, harness or installation included. Manufacturer also sells complete CICs, which have a different accounting boundary.
caveats: The chosen comparison endpoint uses the US AIAA-S111-2005 table at 1E15 1 MeV electrons/cm². ECSS post-anneal factors form a separate case and are not mixed into it.
The header labels 1E14 as 10-yr LEO and 1E15 as 15-yr GEO are generic source annotations. No orbit, shielding or environmental equivalence is supplied, so no mission-year interpretation is adopted.

Absolute irradiated MPP values are explicit arithmetic derivations using separately published Vmp and Jmp retention factors and the documented 27 cm² reference area. They are not fabricated from Pmp retention.
The 2022 sheet changes thickness to 140–225 µm and areal mass to 84–130 mg/cm². Do not use the older search-ranked sheet values 80–225 µm and 50–84 mg/cm².
Mass and thickness retain manufacturer option ranges. No arbitrary midpoint or preferred thin option is selected. The current scalar mass screen cannot consume the mass interval.
The temperature-coefficient table does not explicitly identify which radiation annealing protocol applies. Keep the coefficients as characterized data with that applicability gap visible.
No full I–V or irradiance-dependent curve or equivalent-circuit parameter set is supplied. No DET, shading, cold-start or converter-extrema claim is supported.
Drawing units are unresolved. widthM and heightM remain missing. No centimetre interpretation is adopted. The exact supplier ordering identity and paired thickness/mass option remain unresolved.

products.accountingBoundary: External OBC software process. CPU/RAM/storage, execution power, thermal dissipation and mass belong to the OBC hardware once. The controlled STARBUCK-NANO EPS is a separate hardware usage.
caveats: Narrow service, not internal EPS firmware or a complete EPS power-management law. No MPPT, charge regulator or autonomous load shedding is implemented by this entry.
Maintainer documents KubOS/Linux OBC targets. No specific installed EPS revision, electrical connection or flight qualification is verified.
Service version 0.1.0 in a 2022 preservation snapshot. No independent build or hardware execution was performed.
Watchdog thread ignores kick errors. Sleep(60) is not a guaranteed 60 s period or deadline.
Schema casts i32 parameters to u8 without range validation here. Do not invent validated parameter bounds. noop actually calls reset_watchdog.

supportedConfigurations: Pinned C library and Linux kubos-hal/i2c-dev backend with pthread. Example integration endpoint /dev/i2c-0 at 0x02. Source housekeeping layout labeled P31u-8. Optional Rust wrapper has explicitly retained interface limitations.
products.accountingBoundary: Software-only external OBC library. CPU, physical memory/storage, execution power, mass and thermal dissipation belong to the Linux host hardware once. The controlled P31U EPS remains a separate hardware usage.
caveats: Not internal EPS firmware and not a complete autonomous power-management law. Commands select or configure hardware behavior rather than implementing MPPT or battery regulation locally.
CMake component version is 1.0.0. Rust wrapper crate version is 0.1.0. Both are retained under the pinned commit without manufacturing one unified release number.
Linux deployment is evidenced by actual i2c-dev backend and a source integration client, not by a completed hardware test. No exact tested P31U firmware/hardware revision is established.
Header explicitly modifies the P31u-8 housekeeping layout and counter widths. Installation must verify the actual EPS firmware data layout.
Client uses address 0x02, while Rust constructor prose mentions 0x08. Address is caller supplied. No universal default address is inferred.

Rust wrapper introduces Both heater selection=2, but C rejects selection>1. Rust new passes bus.as_ptr() to C without proving NUL-termination. The primary catalog scope is the actual C interface, not a validated Rust wrapper.
Rust introductory save-unimplemented comment conflicts with its implemented save method and C save function. Saving behavior remains subject to the device protocol and sequencing.
C validates output indices/states, PV mode and heater selector/state, but forwards voltage and configuration fields without establishing safe hardware electrical ranges.
Optional watchdog uses process-global connection state and a pthread. Kick errors are ignored by the worker. No guaranteed task period or thread-safe concurrent command contract is established.
The supplied integration client reconfigures batteries/outputs, controls heaters and resets the EPS. It was reviewed only, never executed.
Header specifies battery-save sequencing 1..30 seconds, while the supplied integration client waits 600 ms before saving. No protocol timing guarantee is inferred.
